patients.summary: Financial analyst in his thirties with ulcerative colitis since 2015 on mesalamine, followed by an outside GI group. Joins in 2022; primary sclerosing cholangitis is found on MRCP in October 2025, and worsening cholestasis in spring 2026 leads to ERCP dilation of a dominant bile duct stricture with negative brushings.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 30M, moving his primary care here. Previous PCP was fine, wanted easier access. Works as a financial analyst, long weeks around quarter close.

UC: diagnosed 2015, around age 23. Has been on mesalamine 1.2 g twice a day ever since. Followed by an outside GI group, sees them about once a year and they do his GI labs. Says he has been in remission a long time, no bleeding, normal stools, no abdominal pain. Takes the mesalamine reliably. GI refills it.

No other medical problems. No surgeries. NKDA.

Family: maternal grandmother had UC. Father has primary sclerosing cholangitis. Mother has autoimmune hypothyroidism.

Social: never smoked, does not drink at all, no drugs. Lives in Easthampton. Exercises a few times a week.

ROS: negative except as above. No fatigue, no itching, no weight change.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. HEENT unremarkable, no scleral icterus. Neck supple, no adenopathy. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema. Skin without rash.

A/P
1. Ulcerative colitis, in remission per patient on mesalamine. Continue with GI. Will request their most recent note. Mesalamine needs renal function checked; doing a BMP today.
2. Health maintenance: CBC, BMP, lipids. HIV and hep C screening today, he agrees. Tdap given, no record of one in the last 10 years. Flu and COVID boosters next month when available. PHQ-2 0.
3. Return in a year for a physical, sooner as needed. He has my cell for questions.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Austin, your blood counts, kidney function, electrolytes and cholesterol all look good. HIV and hepatitis C screens were nonreactive, which is what we expected; no need to repeat those unless something changes. Kidney numbers are the main thing we watch on mesalamine and yours are normal.

documents.title: RE: Your recent lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thanks for the quick turnaround.

Date of service: 10/14/2024

Medications: mesalamine DR 1.2 g by mouth twice daily.

Impression: ulcerative colitis in clinical remission on mesalamine.

conditions.label: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
conditions.note: Diagnosed by outside GI on MRCP.

reports.text:
OUTSIDE IMAGING REPORT
Exam: MRI abdomen without and with contrast, MRCP protocol.
Indication: Cholestatic liver tests in a patient with ulcerative colitis.
Technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MR imaging of the abdomen with 2D and 3D MRCP sequences before and after IV gadolinium.
Findings: Multiple short strictures involve the intrahepatic ducts of both lobes and the extrahepatic bile duct, with intervening segments of dilation. No discrete intraductal filling defect. Liver normal in size and signal without focal lesion. Gallbladder unremarkable. Pancreas normal; pancreatic duct not dilated. Spleen normal in size. No ascites. No lymphadenopathy. Kidneys and adrenals unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Multifocal intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary strictures with segmental dilations, in keeping with primary sclerosing cholangitis.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP
Dates: clinic visit 10/06/2025; MRCP 10/17/2025
Re: Austin Crowley, DOB 04/05/1992

Dear Doctor,

Austin came back to clinic with roughly six months of fatigue and itching. On questioning he also described on-and-off bloody diarrhea going back to late last year, which he had put down to hemorrhoids and had not mentioned to anyone. He continues mesalamine DR 1.2 g twice daily. He denies travel, alcohol or sexual risk exposures.

Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal grandmother with UC, father with PSC, mother with autoimmune hypothyroidism.

Exam: well nourished, jaundiced. Abdomen soft, not distended, nontender. No hepatosplenomegaly. No ascites.

Labs 10/06/2025:
Total bilirubin 2.1 mg/dL (H)
Direct bilirubin 1.5 mg/dL (H)
Alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L (H)
GGT 210 U/L (H)
AST 50 U/L (H)
ALT 55 U/L

MRCP 10/17/2025: multifocal strictures of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts with segmental dilation (report enclosed).

Impression: primary sclerosing cholangitis in a patient with long-standing ulcerative colitis and a father with PSC. Cholestatic liver enzymes with mild hyperbilirubinemia.

Plan: continue mesalamine 1.2 g twice daily. We discussed the diagnosis with him by phone after the MRCP. Follow-up in clinic in six months with repeat labs, sooner if jaundice or itching worsens.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here to go over the new PSC diagnosis. GI letter and MRCP report reviewed with him. He has been tired and itchy since around the spring and figured it was work stress. The bloody stool episodes GI wrote about he had brushed off as hemorrhoids; GI is aware. He knows PSC well from his father and has a lot of questions about what comes next. Still on mesalamine 1.2 g BID. No other meds. NKDA. No alcohol.

O: Vitals as charted, weight unchanged. Sclerae faintly yellow. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly, no ascites. No edema.

A/P:
1. Primary sclerosing cholangitis, new, GI managing. Labs and MRCP reviewed, bilirubin 2.1 and alk phos 420. Talked through how it is usually followed with labs and imaging and that GI will lead. Added to problem list. Asked him to message me or GI right away for fever, worse yellowing, or right-sided belly pain.
2. UC on mesalamine, per GI.
3. Vaccines for chronic liver disease: hep B series already complete (2023). Hep A dose 1 today, dose 2 in 6 months. PCV20 today.
4. Physical still to be rebooked, front desk to schedule December.

~35 minutes, more than half counseling.

Mood ok, a little down about the diagnosis but coping, talking with family. Sleeping fine. PHQ-2 1.

NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: Well appearing, no distress. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema. Skin with no rash.

Plan:
- PSC and UC per GI. Liver labs with GI in the spring, not repeating here.
- BMP for mesalamine, CBC.
- Vaccines: flu, COVID done this fall. PCV20 and hep A #1 given 11/4; hep A #2 due May.
- RTC 1 year, or sooner.

reports.text:
OUTSIDE IMAGING REPORT
Exam: Ultrasound, abdomen complete.
Indication: Primary sclerosing cholangitis, rising bilirubin.
Findings: The intrahepatic bile ducts are beaded and irregular. The liver is normal in size without focal mass. Gallbladder is normal, without stones or wall thickening. Visualized pancreas unremarkable. Spleen normal in size. Both kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Abdominal aorta normal caliber. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Beading and irregularity of the intrahepatic bile ducts, consistent with known primary sclerosing cholangitis.

Dear Doctor,

Austin returned six months after we diagnosed primary sclerosing cholangitis. Fatigue and itching have persisted through the winter and he has been yellow off and on. Over the last stretch he has noticed pale stools and dark urine. His colitis has stayed quiet on mesalamine, and the bleeding episodes he described last fall have not come back.

Medications: mesalamine DR 1.2 g twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal grandmother UC, father PSC, mother autoimmune hypothyroidism.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, financial analyst.

Exam: afebrile. Sclerae icteric. Abdomen soft, not distended, no masses, mildly tender in the right upper quadrant.

Labs 04/20/2026:
Total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL (H)
Direct bilirubin 2.5 mg/dL (H)
Alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L (H)
AST 80 U/L (H)
ALT 75 U/L (H)
CA 19-9 22 U/mL (normal)

Abdominal ultrasound today: beaded, irregular intrahepatic ducts (report enclosed).

Impression: PSC with worsening cholestasis and jaundice; concern for a dominant stricture. CA 19-9 reassuring.
Plan: ERCP with cholangiography, possible dilation and brushings, being scheduled at the regional hospital. Continue mesalamine.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.

reports.text:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL ENDOSCOPY
Procedure: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography with biliary balloon dilation and brushings.
Indication: Primary sclerosing cholangitis with rising bilirubin, pale stools and dark urine.
Sedation: Monitored anesthesia care.
Findings: Normal major papilla. Deep biliary cannulation achieved. Cholangiogram shows multifocal intrahepatic strictures with intervening dilation, and a dominant stricture of the common bile duct. Biliary sphincterotomy not performed. The dominant stricture was dilated with a balloon. Brushings of the stricture sent for cytology. Good drainage of contrast after dilation. No stent placed. Pancreatic duct not opacified.
Complications: None.
Disposition: Discharged home the same day.
reports.conclusion: Dominant common bile duct stricture in primary sclerosing cholangitis, balloon dilated; brushings obtained; no stent.

documents.title: ERCP Procedure Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Regional hospital endoscopy report, procedure date 05/12/2026, received by fax.

ERCP for PSC with worsening cholestasis. Dominant common bile duct stricture identified and balloon dilated; brushings sent to cytology. No stent. No complications. Discharged home same day with his family. Mesalamine to continue. Clinic follow-up with labs in about six weeks.

Allergies: NKDA.

reports.text:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL PATHOLOGY
Specimen: Common bile duct stricture, brushings.
Clinical history: Primary sclerosing cholangitis, dominant stricture.
Adequacy: Satisfactory for evaluation.
Microscopic: Cellular specimen with benign ductal epithelium in flat sheets. No atypical or malignant cells identified.

documents.title: Bile Duct Brushing Cytology
documents.author: pathology
documents.body: Cytology report from the regional hospital for the 05/12/2026 ERCP brushings: benign ductal cells, negative for malignancy. Copy also sent to ordering gastroenterologist. Scanned to chart. -- MA
